info.bio: Surgen en Nueva York, al mismo tiempo que los Ramones (podría decirse que son primos hermanos). Canciones cortas, impactantes, pero con alguna variedad en los ritmos. Apoyan su fuerza, sobre todo en el escenario, en la extraordinaria voz de Manitoba (el guapo) y en la guitarra absolutamente bestial de Ross the Boss. Tienen una larga carrera, pero pocos discos, aunque todos merecen la pena.

scenes.name: Decadencia y glam-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El rock siempre tuvo un elemento de decadencia, amoralidad y obscenidad; entre los Cockettes (1968) y el Rocky Horror Picture Show (1974) se convierte en producto de masas. Gran Bretaña lo llama glam-rock: T.Rex lo inaugura y lo casa con el hard rock; David Bowie lo lleva a su cima comercial convirtiendo el marketing en arte (Ziggy Stardust, la trilogía berlinesa con Eno). En EE UU, Alice Cooper, Sparks, Iggy Pop y Lou Reed (Berlin, Metal Machine Music, New York). El glam y la decadencia preparan el punk: Mott The Hoople, Be Bop Deluxe, New York Dolls, Heartbreakers, Dictators, Modern Lovers de Jonathan Richman, Runaways.

podcast.title: Inspiration for "Punk" Fanzine Name
podcast.body: The Dictators were a band from Manhattan's "scusy scene" whose album art for "The Dictators Go Girl Crazy" (1975) showed all four members in leather jackets at a hamburger stand. This image led fan Legs McNeill to exclaim that they looked like a "bunch of... punks," prompting him to rename his fanzine to "Punk," thus solidifying the term for the genre. "Inside was a shot of all four members of the band wearing leather jackets at a hamburger stand. And legs thought they all look like a bunch of... punks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for "Punk" Magazine Name
podcast.body: The Dictators' 1975 album "Go Girl Crazy" featured an inside picture of the band at a White Castle, dressed in black leather jackets, evoking the image of 1950s "punks" like Marlon Brando and James Dean. This image directly inspired the fanzine's authors to name their publication "Punk," thus making The Dictators historically significant as the band who inspired the word used to describe a new form of stripped-down rock and roll. "Instead, they got inspired by a picture of another New York band called The Dictators... And the Dictators? Well, they've gone down in history as the band who inspired the word, to describe a brand new form of stripped down rock and roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for Punk Magazine
podcast.body: The Dictators were the favorite band of Legs McNeil in the mid-1970s New York underground music scene. His desire to find an excuse to spend time with them led him to conceive of starting a fanzine, which he hoped would provide a legitimate reason to meet and interview the band, or perhaps gain free entry to shows and drinks. "His favorite band of them all was the dictators, and he wanted to come up with an excuse to hang out with them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performance During CBGB's Final Weeks
podcast.body: The Dictators were among the bands that performed at CBGB during its final weeks before the club closed down in October 2006. "The final weeks featured bands like Bad Brains, The Dictators, and even Blondie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Covered in "Punk" Fanzine
xref.body: Television was identified as one of the "new groups that were sprouting up in New York" that Legs McNeill featured in his "Punk" fanzine. As the scene around CBGBs expanded, the fanzine documented these emerging artists, including Television. "Legs wrote about the Dictators. He wrote about Iggy Pop and Lou Reed and television and all the other new groups that were sprouting up in New York at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Featured in Punk Magazine
xref.body: The fanzine "Punk," which appeared at the end of 1975, was dedicated to groups like The Ramones, who appeared at CBGB, helping to define the "punk artist" label for bands in the burgeoning scene. "This fanzine was dedicated to singers like Lou Reed and groups like the Ramones, who appeared at CBGB."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
